strings.d1.theme: Louvre, Tuileries and the Eiffel Tower
strings.d1.s0.name: Louvre Müzesi
strings.d1.s0.tips: Head straight for the Mona Lisa, then the Denon wing. Book a timed ticket online (32 EUR for non-EU visitors); the Carrousel entrance has no queue.
strings.d1.s1.name: Jardin des Tuileries
strings.d1.s1.tips: Stroll through the gardens from the Louvre to Concorde, and grab one of the green chairs.
strings.d1.s2.name: Café Kitsuné Palais Royal
strings.d1.s2.tips: Coffee and a sandwich in the Palais Royal garden, set in a colonnaded courtyard.
strings.d1.s3.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
strings.d1.s3.tips: Monet's Water Lilies in oval rooms. Right next to the Louvre and calm.
strings.d1.s4.name: Eiffel Tower
strings.d1.s4.tips: Take the stairs to the 2nd floor, then the lift to the summit (about 29 EUR). Book online, go at sunset, and take photos from Trocadéro.
strings.d1.b0.name: Le Petit Cler
strings.d1.b0.tips: A bistro on Rue Cler, close to the Eiffel Tower.
strings.d1.b1.name: Champ de Mars
strings.d1.b1.tips: Lawns beneath the tower: picnic here and watch the light show (every hour on the hour).
strings.d2.theme: Île de la Cité, Latin Quarter and Saint-Germain
strings.d2.s0.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
strings.d2.s0.tips: The restored cathedral is free; reserve a time slot online. Mornings are quiet.
strings.d2.s1.name: Sainte-Chapelle
strings.d2.s1.tips: 1,113 stained-glass panels, loveliest on a sunny morning. Book online.
strings.d2.s2.name: Shakespeare and Company
strings.d2.s2.tips: The legendary English-language bookshop on the Seine.
strings.d2.s3.name: Le Comptoir du Panthéon
strings.d2.s3.tips: A bistro opposite the Panthéon, with steak-frites and a terrace.
strings.d2.s4.name: Panthéon
strings.d2.s4.tips: The tombs of Voltaire, Hugo and Curie, plus the Foucault pendulum.
strings.d2.b0.name: Bouillon Racine
strings.d2.b0.tips: An Art Nouveau bouillon with a cheap, classic French menu.
strings.d2.b1.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
strings.d2.b1.tips: The Senate gardens, with a pond and chairs. Go here instead of the Panthéon.
strings.d3.s0.name: Sacré-Cœur
strings.d3.s0.tips: The basilica is free; the dome costs 8 EUR. The steps are empty in the morning, with views over Paris.
strings.d3.s1.name: Place du Tertre
strings.d3.s1.tips: The painters' square. Portraits cost 40-60 EUR, and the price is negotiable.
strings.d3.s2.name: Montmartre Vineyard and Lapin Agile
strings.d3.s2.tips: Paris's last vineyard and a cabaret, on Rue des Saules.
strings.d3.s3.name: Chantoiseau Montmartre
strings.d3.s3.tips: A neo-bistro 7 minutes from Place du Tertre, with a set lunch menu.
strings.d3.s4.name: Musée de Montmartre
strings.d3.s4.tips: Renoir's studio and gardens, with views over the vineyard.
strings.d3.b0.name: Boulangerie Pain Pain
strings.d3.b0.tips: Award-winning baguettes and pastries for a quick lunch.
strings.d3.b1.name: Moulin Rouge
strings.d3.b1.tips: See it from outside in Pigalle; the evening show is extra (about 120 EUR).
strings.d4.s0.name: Place des Vosges
strings.d4.s0.tips: The oldest square in Paris, with arcades and Victor Hugo's house (free).
strings.d4.s1.name: Musée Picasso Paris
strings.d4.s1.tips: The Picasso collection in the Hôtel Salé. Book online.
strings.d4.s2.name: L'As du Fallafel
strings.d4.s2.tips: The falafel place on Rue des Rosiers with the queue outside. Eat standing up.
strings.d4.s3.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
strings.d4.s3.tips: The oldest market in Paris, with Moroccan, Japanese and Lebanese stalls.
strings.d4.s4.name: Centre Pompidou
strings.d4.s4.tips: Inside-out architecture, modern art and a terrace with views over Paris. It is under renovation 2025-30: if closed, go to the Bourse de Commerce.
strings.d4.b0.name: Bourse de Commerce Pinault Collection
strings.d4.b0.tips: Tadao Ando's concrete cylinder, with contemporary art. Go here if the Pompidou is closed.
strings.d4.b1.name: Au Petit Versailles du Marais
strings.d4.b1.tips: Award-winning croissants and quiche. Go here instead of the falafel.
strings.d5.s0.name: Musée d'Orsay
strings.d5.s0.tips: Impressionists in a former railway station. Van Gogh is on the 5th floor; take a photo through the clock face. Book online.
strings.d5.s1.name: Rue du Bac & Bon Marché
strings.d5.s1.tips: The Grande Épicerie food hall, good for souvenirs.
strings.d5.s2.name: Café de Flore
strings.d5.s2.tips: Saint-Germain's literary café: croque monsieur and hot chocolate.
strings.d5.s3.name: Pont des Arts and the Seine Banks
strings.d5.s3.tips: See Île de la Cité from the bridge, then walk along the riverside path.
strings.d5.s4.name: Bateaux Parisiens Seine Cruise
strings.d5.s4.tips: A 1-hour river cruise from the Eiffel Tower pier, with Notre-Dame and the Eiffel Tower in sunset light.
strings.d5.b0.name: Bateaux Mouches
strings.d5.b0.tips: The other cruise company, at Pont de l'Alma.
strings.d5.b1.name: La Grande Épicerie de Paris
strings.d5.b1.tips: The food hall at Bon Marché. Have lunch at the counters instead of Café de Flore.
strings.d6.s0.name: Palace of Versailles
strings.d6.s0.tips: 45 minutes on the RER C. Get the palace + gardens + Trianon passport (about 32 EUR). The Hall of Mirrors is empty at the 09:00 opening.
strings.d6.s1.name: Gardens of Versailles
strings.d6.s1.tips: The gardens are free in winter. The fountains are off, so just walk.
strings.d6.s2.name: La Flottille Versailles
strings.d6.s2.tips: A restaurant on the Grand Canal, with boat rental next door.
strings.d6.s3.name: Petit Trianon & Queen's Hamlet
strings.d6.s3.tips: Marie Antoinette's village and the queen's farm, included with the passport.
strings.d6.s4.name: Marché Notre-Dame Versailles
strings.d6.s4.tips: A food market in town: pick up cheese on your way back.
strings.d6.b0.name: Angelina Versailles
strings.d6.b0.tips: Hot chocolate and Mont-Blanc inside the palace.
strings.d6.b1.name: Grand Trianon
strings.d6.b1.tips: A pink marble pavilion. Go here instead of the Petit Trianon.
strings.d7.theme: Canal Saint-Martin and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Canal Saint-Martin
strings.d7.s0.tips: Iron footbridges and canal locks. Have a morning coffee and spot the Amélie film scenes.
strings.d7.s1.name: Du Pain et des Idées
strings.d7.s1.tips: One of the best bakeries in Paris. Try the pistachio-chocolate escargot.
strings.d7.s2.name: Marché d'Aligre
strings.d7.s2.tips: A daily market at Bastille, with cheese and edible souvenirs.
strings.d7.s3.name: Le Baron Rouge
strings.d7.s3.tips: A wine bar next to the Aligre market. Oysters and wine from the barrel make a fitting farewell.
strings.d7.s4.name: Gare du Nord
strings.d7.s4.tips: 35 minutes to CDG on the RER B. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Holybelly Canal
strings.d7.b1.name: Coulée Verte René-Dumont
strings.d7.b1.tips: A green walkway on a former railway line. Go here instead of Aligre.
strings.note0: Use a Navigo Easy with a t+ carnet on the metro, the RER C for Versailles and the RER B for CDG (11 EUR). The city is walkable: skip the metro for 20-minute distances.
strings.note1: Timed online tickets are essential for the Louvre, Orsay and Sainte-Chapelle. The Louvre is closed on Tuesdays and Orsay on Mondays. The Paris Museum Pass covers 2 to 6 days.
strings.note2: Winter temperatures are 3-8°C and it is dark by 17:00. Museums are quiet, with Christmas windows (Galeries Lafayette) and mulled wine markets in December.
strings.note3: Bistro lunch menus (formule) cost 18-25 EUR, half the evening price. Tap water (carafe d'eau) is free; round up the bill as a tip.
strings.note4: Bouillons (Chartier, Racine) are cheap classics. Go to the Marais for falafel, and to Pain Pain or Du Pain et des Idées for croissants.
strings.note5: Watch out for pickpockets on metro line 1 and in Montmartre. Wear your backpack on your front.
strings.transit.name: Navigo Easy / t+ carnet
strings.transit.why_chosen: Covers the metro, RER and buses. The 10-ticket carnet is the most practical option; Versailles needs an extra RER C ticket.
